items.summary: T-cell exhaustion limits durable antitumor responses and remains a barrier to adoptive cell transfer (ACT) therapies in solid tumors. items.title: Tumor-intrinsic and extrinsic immune mechanisms define resistance to immune checkpoint blockade in metastatic melanoma [tcr]
items.summary: The interplay between variable genomic, transcriptional, and microenvironmental features driving resistance to immune checkpoint blockade (ICB) remains poorly understood. Here, we performed multi-omic profiling (single-nucleus RNA, T cell receptor, and whole-genome sequencing) of 42 sequential biopsies from 34 patients with metastatic melanoma. Using a Bayesian integrative model, we identify recurring features of ICB-sensitive and resistant clones, and uncouple gene dosage effects from transcriptional output, thereby defining genetic and non-genetic basis for plasticity. items.title: Long-term confinement triggers RIPK3-independent necroptosis in amoeboid cancer cells to shape tumor evolution
items.summary: The mesenchymal–amoeboid transition (MAT) confers enhanced migratory capacity and therapy resistance to cancer cells. items.title: Compartment-specific PPARδ activity controls the outcome of cancer – immune cell competition and immunotherapy efficacy
items.summary: Most patients with solid tumors fail to sustain anti-tumor immunity, in part because immune cells cannot outcompete cancer cells inside the immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment. Here, we identify the lipid-sensing transcription factor PPARδ as a compartment-specific determinant of cancer-immune fitness balance and immunotherapy efficacy. items.title: Integrated spatial and single cell analysis identifies CCL21+ lymphatic endothelial cells as a driver of a favorable immune environment in acral melanoma
items.summary: Acral melanoma (AM) is a rare type of melanoma that responds poorly to immunotherapy. In the current study we undertook integrated single cell RNA-Seq, spatial transcriptomics and multiplexed immunofluorescence to identify potential regulators of the immune environment. Our analyses identified distinct immune habitats at the invasive front, intratumoral regions and areas of distant inflammation across the AM samples. items.title: Neoadjuvant Pepinemab with Immune Checkpoint Blockade Remodels the Tumor Microenvironment in Metastatic Melanoma
items.summary: Neoadjuvant immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) improve event-free survival in metastatic melanoma, yet resistance and recurrence remain common. We evaluated pepinemab, a Semaphorin 4D (SEMA4D)–blocking antibody, in combination with nivolumab and/or ipilimumab in a phase II neoadjuvant biomarker trial for patients with resectable metastatic melanoma. Patients received two neoadjuvant doses followed by curative-intent surgery and one year of adjuvant nivolumab. items.title: Antibodies derived from patient tumors augment response to immune checkpoint blockade in cancer
items.summary: B-cells are associated with favorable response to immunotherapy, though the underlying mechanisms remain unclear. Here, we profiled tumor-infiltrating B-cells (TIL-Bs) and tertiary lymphoid structures (TLS) from α-PD-1 + α-CTLA-4 treated responders (R) and non-responders (NR) to identify immune signatures. TLS from responders exhibited upregulated inflammatory genes, and increased levels of cytotoxic immune cells.

items.summary: The immune microenvironment of classical Hodgkin lymphoma (cHL) is characterized by rare Hodgkin–Reed–Sternberg cells surrounded by dysfunctional lymphocytes, with support from PD-1/PD-L1 interactions. items.title: Divergent Cytotoxic and Inflammatory Functions of Intratumoral Vd2+ gdT Cells in Renal Cell Carcinoma
items.summary: We characterized Vd2+ gdT cell subsets in paired peripheral blood and tumor samples from three treatment-naive clear cell renal cell carcinoma (ccRCC) patients using flow cytometry and single-cell RNA sequencing. Two major subsets distinguished by CD16 expression exhibited divergent cytotoxic and inflammatory effector programs within the tumor microenvironment. Single-cell RNA sequencing identified four transcriptional clusters with a TOX+ progenitor-like cluster giving rise to divergent effector states.

items.title: PLA2G2D in tumour-draining lymph nodes regulates anti-tumour immunity
